newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Golf-Woosnam decides against surgery on his back.
newsitem.headline: Golf-Woosnam decides against surgery on his back.

text.p: Former US Masters champion Ian Woosnam said on Tuesday that he would "live with the pain" of his bad back rather than undergo surgery.
The world number 28, runner-up to Colin Montgomerie in this year's European Tour order of merit, said he had seen a specialist who advised against an operation.

"The specialist told me I will just have to live with the pain," he said. "I have a vertebra that wants coming out, but it can wait for two or three years. I am going to keep on playing and put up with the spasms and back pain.
"My main problem is muscular and the doctor reckons I have got to live with it and take whatever he gives me for the pain," Woosnam said.
The 38-year-old Welshman is competing in the Johnnie Walker Super Tour with European number one Colin Montgomerie, Ernie Els, world ranked three, Fiji's Vijay Singh and four leading Asian players.
The 72-hole event teed off at the Ta Shee Golf Club in Taipei on Tuesday morning. Other rounds are to be played in Seoul, Manila and Bangkok over the next six days.
